d72f1eec-04cb-45b2-aaa1-6cdc2aee61a7.customer_canonical: The Mayor and Commonalty and Citizens of the City of London
d72f1eec-04cb-45b2-aaa1-6cdc2aee61a7.explanation: Buyer-side found the target organisation matched to Phoenix Software Ltd under framework Y23065 (CAA_ONLY, no COA), but supplier-side reports on Softcat PLC spend for the same framework. The two nodes appear to be describing different supplier relationships, and the supplier verdict contains unresolved date inconsistencies (current date 2026-07-09 with a "last spend entry" of Mar 27, which is in the future). Cross-evidence conflict and supplier verdict unreliability warrant case review before any rebate determination.

buyer_evidence.ambiguity_note: The input specified supplier "Softcat Plc" but the only matching row found for this organisation (canonical match "mayor commonalty citizens of city of london" vs input "mayor and commonalty and citizens of city of london") under framework Y23065 lists supplier as "Phoenix Software Ltd", not Softcat. No row exists pairing this exact organisation name with Softcat as supplier under Y23065 (a separate organisation "City of London Corporation" has multiple Softcat-supplied YES/YES rows, but that is a distinct legal entity name and was not treated as a match per instructions not to conflate similar-but-different organisation names). Additionally, no narrative Notes/Updates or Rebate Related Notes text was present in any candidate row's data (notes fields were null throughout), so the verdict rests solely on the structured CAA?/COA? columns for the row 845 match, which reads CAA=YES, COA=NO.
buyer_evidence.evidence_excerpt: No notes text was provided in the source data for this row; only structured field values were available: customerRaw "The Mayor Commonalty Citizens of the city of London", supplierRaw "Phoenix Software Ltd", frameworkRaw "Software Y23065", coaStatus "NO", caaStatus "YES".

supplier_evidence.evidence_excerpt: Softcat PLC (canonical: softcat) appears in Backdated Spend log row 7 with Y23065 framework spend of £89,400 (rebate £670.50) reported for Mar 27. Framework Y23065 (Software Products & Associated Services) has monthly reporting frequency per Framework Rules row 47. Current date: 2026-07-09, which falls within the valid framework period (2023-03-31 to 2027-03-30). Most recent expected reporting month is Mar 27 (3 months prior to current Jul 26 cycle date). Entry exists in expected due month → ON_SCHEDULE.

judge_result.cross_evidence_conflict_note: The two nodes match on different suppliers for the same framework Y23065. Buyer-side explicitly found NO row pairing the target organisation with Softcat under Y23065 — the matching row (Opportunity 845) lists the supplier as "Phoenix Software Ltd," and the buyer node deliberately declined to treat the separate "City of London Corporation"/Softcat rows as the same entity. Supplier-side, however, reports on Softcat PLC spend under Y23065 as if it corresponds to the same engagement. Read together, the buyer verdict says the target org's Y23065 contract is with Phoenix Software (CAA_ONLY, no Softcat match), while the supplier verdict evaluates Softcat spend — the two are not describing the same supplier relationship, so the ON_SCHEDULE supplier finding may pertain to a different (or unmatched) contract than the buyer-side CAA_ONLY finding.
judge_result.supplier_evidence_fail_reason: The verdict's date reasoning is internally inconsistent and the "on schedule" conclusion is not supported. The excerpt states the current date is 2026-07-09 (Jul 26 cycle), yet the last spend entry is "Mar 27" — a month that is in the FUTURE relative to the stated current date, which is impossible for a reported spend entry. The reasoning further claims "Most recent expected reporting month is Mar 27 (3 months prior to current Jul 26 cycle date)," which is arithmetically wrong: Mar 27 is not prior to Jul 26, it is after it. For monthly reporting with a current date of 2026-07-09, the expected most-recent month should be around Jun 26, not Mar 27. The ON_SCHEDULE verdict therefore rests on contradictory dates and cannot be verified as sound; the node should be retried to reconcile the current date, the last-entry month, and the monthly cadence.

judge_result.cross_evidence_conflict_note: The two nodes match on different suppliers for the same framework Y23065. Buyer-side explicitly found NO row pairing the target organisation with Softcat under Y23065 — the matching row (Opportunity 845) lists the supplier as "Phoenix Software Ltd," and the buyer node deliberately declined to treat the separate "City of London Corporation"/Softcat rows as the same entity. Supplier-side, however, reports on Softcat PLC spend under Y23065 as if it corresponds to the same engagement. Read together, the buyer verdict says the target org's Y23065 contract is with Phoenix Software (CAA_ONLY, no Softcat match), while the supplier verdict evaluates Softcat spend — the two are not describing the same supplier relationship, so the ON_SCHEDULE supplier finding may pertain to a different (or unmatched) contract than the buyer-side CAA_ONLY finding.
judge_result.supplier_evidence_fail_reason: The verdict's date reasoning is internally inconsistent and the "on schedule" conclusion is not supported. The excerpt states the current date is 2026-07-09 (Jul 26 cycle), yet the last spend entry is "Mar 27" — a month that is in the FUTURE relative to the stated current date, which is impossible for a reported spend entry. The reasoning further claims "Most recent expected reporting month is Mar 27 (3 months prior to current Jul 26 cycle date)," which is arithmetically wrong: Mar 27 is not prior to Jul 26, it is after it. For monthly reporting with a current date of 2026-07-09, the expected most-recent month should be around Jun 26, not Mar 27. The ON_SCHEDULE verdict therefore rests on contradictory dates and cannot be verified as sound; the node should be retried to reconcile the current date, the last-entry month, and the monthly cadence.
